body:
As discussed on Slack, it would be wonderful if ASVS had a stated reference standard. I had asked:

> Is there a standard or preferred way of referencing ASVS controls? Ex: combination of ASVS release/milestone version and shortcode?

And subsequently suggested the example: `v4.0.1-1.1.3`
Which breaksdown as `v<version_number>-<requirement_number>`

@tghosth @vanderaj @jmanico @danielcuthbert if we can get some consensus on this I'd be glad to create a PR for the repo's README to document it.

Having this established will help other projects reference ASVS requirements.

<sub>Side note: Also from Slack, consistency in whether they are 'requirements' or 'controls' would also be something to keep in mind for the future 👍 </sub>

comments.body:
> And subsequently suggested the example: `v4.0.1-1.1.3`
> Which breaksdown as `v<version_number>-<requirement_number>`

I like this
@vanderaj @jmanico @danielcuthbert any thoughts? Agreement? Disagreement?
What is the use-case for this?
Cross referencing between ASVS and other tools/docs.

I could be done in such as way that using versioned references are encouraged but not technically required. Similar to: 
- https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/#how-to-reference-wstg-scenarios
- https://github.com/OWASP/wstg/pull/472

(If that's a concern/blocker for anyone.)

It's been months, it'd be really nice to get some feedback on this and have it documented. So that people and other projects can move forward referencing ASVS in a formalized manner.

@vanderaj @jmanico @danielcuthbert any thoughts? Agreement? Disagreement?

This seems fairly mild, I see no reason why not to move forward on this.

For for it @kingthorin if you want an early review before you put to 
much work into it let me know.

Aloha,

-- 
Jim Manico
Manicode Security
https://www.manicode.com

Hi @kingthorin. I'm still between jobs, so if you want me to help, or set something up with me (vanderaj@owasp.org) to discuss further, happy to do so. This would definitely be a 4.1 or later change, but I am in full support. We have had similar discussions in the OWASP Top 10 @sslhello @infosecdad @neilsmithline

I think we refer to "chapters" and "segments" based on the wording from here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x02-Preface.md

Did you get category/sub-category from somewhere in particular?
And we should usually mention "requirement" rather than "control"
Thanks @tghosth category/sub-category were totally out of thin air. I'll tweak that as you suggested too.
I also think we should use v4.0.1-1.11.3 rather than v401-1.11.3
Fair enough, that was a holdover from the WSTG text where we were trying to avoid periods. Since ASVS identifiers already include them it'll have to be dealt with anyway.
See PR might be ready to go
For 4.0.2, I will be normalizing our usage of V, but 4.1 can go further if more changes are required.

To add [this](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS#how-to-reference-asvs-requirements) to the document do you want to PR against `4.0.2` or `master`?

Also are we in agreement that it should be inserted in `0x03-Using-ASVS.md` after "Applying ASVS in Practice"?
<sub>(Which makes me notice that you need to standardize headings either with or without Title Caps... topic for another ticket :wink:)</sub>
There was some more discussion on this which will change things slightly, also in relation to #812. I will get on that in next week or so.
See https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/812#issuecomment-657759067
